laptop.definition: a portable computer that can be used on a lap.
examples: She bought a new laptop for school.

launch.definition: to start or set in motion; to release or start something like a project.
examples: The company launched the new app yesterday.

library.definition: a place where books, magazines, and other materials are kept for public use.
examples: I borrowed a book from the library.
She bought a large bottle of juice.

literature.definition: written works, especially those considered to have artistic value.
examples: We read classical literature in class.

lovely.definition: delightful or charming in appearance or manner.
examples: She wore a lovely scarf.

lamp.definition: A device that emits light to illuminate a room or area.
examples: The lamp on the desk brightened the workspace.
She added a warm glow with a small bedside lamp.

lad.definition: A boy or young man; a male youth.
examples: The lad helped his grandfather in the garden.

laconic.definition: Using very few words; concise to the point of seeming rude.
examples: Her laconic reply ended the discussion quickly.

law.definition: The system of rules that governs behavior and enforces penalties.
examples: He studied law to become a lawyer.

lyrical.definition: Expressing the writer's emotions in a beautiful, musical way; poetic.
examples: Her lyrics are lyrical and moving.

lanky.definition: tall and thin, often awkward in appearance
examples: As a kid, he was lanky.
The lanky runner looked fast.

lawyer.definition: a person who gives legal advice and represents people in court
examples: The lawyer explained the contract.
She hired a lawyer for the case.

lambent.definition: glowing softly, usually in a gentle and calm way
examples: The lambent light moved across the wall.
The lamp gave off a lambent glow.

learned.definition: having a lot of knowledge or studying many subjects
examples: He is learned in history.
The learned professor gave a clear answer.

lean.definition: thin and not having much extra fat
examples: She is lean and strong.
He looks lean after training.

lean.definition: to bend your body so you are not straight, often supported by something
examples: I leaned against the wall.
The car leaned to one side.

lank.definition: to become longer and thinner, especially by growing quickly
examples: The plant began to lank toward the light.

lank.definition: a long thin part of something, especially a stretched piece
examples: He tied the lank around the package.

lugubrious.definition: very sad in a gloomy or exaggerated way
examples: His lugubrious voice annoyed everyone.
The movie had a lugubrious ending.
The curtains are lilac.
She wore lilac nail polish.

lilac.definition: a shrub with fragrant purple flowers, or the flowers themselves
examples: A lilac bush is in the front yard.
The lilacs smell sweet in spring.
She was livid about the mistake.
He looked livid when he saw the bill.

luring.definition: Attracting or tempting someone, sometimes in an unfair or dangerous way
examples: The luring advertisement brought many customers.
He warned me about the luring scam calls.

librarian.definition: A person who works in a library and helps people find books and information
examples: The librarian helped me find a book on astronomy.
She works as a librarian at the university.

limp.definition: A way of walking with difficulty due to pain in the leg or foot
examples: He was left with a limp after the accident.
The dog had a limp but still followed us.

limp.definition: To walk with difficulty because of pain or weakness
examples: She limped to the car after twisting her ankle.
He limped home in the rain.
She gave a lucid explanation of the results.
The instructions are lucid and well organized.

lucency.definition: The quality of being clear and easy to understand, or the property of letting light pass through
examples: The presentation improved in lucency after edits.
The material’s lucency made it glow softly.

luster.definition: A shiny attractive quality, especially of something reflecting light
examples: The metal kept its luster after polishing.
The gem’s luster made it stand out.

luminescence.definition: The emission of light by a substance, without heat from burning
examples: Fireflies create luminescence in the dark.
Some minerals show luminescence under ultraviolet light.

ledger.definition: A book or computer record that keeps financial accounts and transactions
examples: The accountant entered the transactions in the ledger.
Errors were found in the company’s ledger.

litigation.definition: the process of taking a legal dispute to court
examples: The company is facing litigation.
Litigation can be expensive and slow.

litigator.definition: a lawyer who handles lawsuits and legal cases
examples: The litigator argued the case in court.
She became a litigator after law school.

lithe.definition: light, flexible, and graceful in movement
examples: She was lithe and moved easily.
The dancer looked lithe and strong.

litigant.definition: a person or group involved in a lawsuit
examples: Both litigants presented their arguments.
The litigant asked for more time.
I’m leery of deals that seem too good.
She was leery after the first scam.

lunge.definition: to move suddenly forward or to one side with a big effort
examples: He lunged to catch the ball.
The dog lunged at the fence.
We used a lidded container to store the food.
The lidded pot kept the heat in.

luminance.definition: the brightness of light in a specific area
examples: The display’s luminance improved in sunlight.
Luminance affects how readable the screen is.

lurid.definition: shockingly vivid, often in a way that seems sensational or unpleasant
examples: The article described a lurid crime scene.
He avoided lurid details in the report.

lustrous.definition: shiny and bright, with a smooth rich appearance
examples: The lustrous coat reflected the light.
Her lustrous hair looked healthy.

limpid.definition: clear and easy to see through; not cloudy
examples: The limpid water reflected the trees.
Her limpid explanation made everything simple.

lamentation.definition: sad and often loud expression of grief
examples: The funeral included lamentation and prayers.
Her lamentation filled the room with sadness.

logography.definition: a writing system where symbols represent words or morphemes
examples: Logography is different from alphabetic writing.
In logography, each symbol can carry meaning.

luminous.definition: giving off light or shining clearly
examples: The luminous sign was visible from far away.
Fireflies are luminous at night.

leer.definition: to look in a way that seems rude, threatening, or sexually suggestive
examples: He leered at the stranger and was asked to leave.
She avoided his leer and walked away.

litigate.definition: to take a legal dispute to court
examples: They decided to litigate instead of settling.
The case was litigated over three years.
She wrote a laudatory review of the book.
The speech was full of laudatory remarks.
He acts like a lout when he interrupts people.
Don’t be a lout; speak politely.

liberate.definition: to set someone free from imprisonment, control, or oppression
examples: They liberated the prisoners after the war.
The movement aimed to liberate people from unfair rules.

loquacious.definition: talking a lot; tending to speak too much
examples: He is loquacious and rarely stops talking.
The interview became loquacious after the first question.

lateralization.definition: the process of developing functions mainly on one side of the brain
examples: Lateralization can affect language processing.
Researchers studied lateralization in brain activity.
